title: Largest 1-Bordered Square
description: Given a 2D binary matrix `grid` of `0`s and `1`s, return the **number of elements (area)** in the largest contiguous square subgrid that has all `1`s on its **border** (all four sides consist exclusively of `1`s; interior cells may be `0` or `1`). Return `0` if no such subgrid exists.
hints: Precompute two tables: hor[r][c] = consecutive 1s ending at (r, c) moving right, and ver[r][c] = consecutive 1s ending at (r, c) moving down.

For each bottom-right corner (r, c), test candidate side lengths s from min(hor[r][c], ver[r][c]) down to best + 1; the top and left sides are valid iff hor[r - s + 1][c] >= s and ver[r][c - s + 1] >= s.

examples.explanation: The entire 3x3 grid has 1s around its border (despite the 0 in the center), so the largest area is 3 * 3 = 9.
The largest 1-bordered square has side length 1, giving area 1.
There are no 1s in the grid, so the largest area is 0.
